claim_recovery_table.claim: SparseTrack reduces ID switches compared to ByteTrack through hierarchical depth-based association
claim_recovery_table.evidence: NEGATIVE - SparseTrack L3 has 3733 ID switches vs ByteTrack 2151 vs SORT 758

claim_recovery_table.claim: SparseTrack achieves higher MOTA than ByteTrack in dense occlusion scenarios
claim_recovery_table.evidence: NEGATIVE - SparseTrack L3 MOTA=0.388 vs ByteTrack MOTA=0.598 vs SORT MOTA=0.818

claim_recovery_table.claim: Pseudo-depth decomposition creates sparser association problems within each layer
claim_recovery_table.evidence: SUPPORTED - Depth layering partitions 200 objects into ~67 per layer (L=3), reducing per-layer association complexity

claim_recovery_table.claim: Increasing depth layers beyond optimal point degrades performance due to over-fragmentation
claim_recovery_table.evidence: SUPPORTED - MOTA decreases monotonically from L1 (0.598) to L10 (0.125)

claim_recovery_table.claim: ByteTrack two-stage association outperforms single-stage SORT when using appropriate score thresholds
claim_recovery_table.evidence: MIXED - With score_threshold=0.1, ByteTrack equals SORT (MOTA=0.818). With higher thresholds, ByteTrack degrades.

claim_recovery_table.claim: SORT achieves highest MOTA due to using all detections with a single association stage
claim_recovery_table.evidence: SUPPORTED - SORT with score_threshold=0.1 achieves MOTA=0.818, outperforming all other configurations

claim_recovery_table.claim: SparseTrack maintains higher Mostly Tracked count than ByteTrack
claim_recovery_table.evidence: SUPPORTED - SparseTrack L3 MT=200 vs ByteTrack MT=167 (at score_threshold=0.2)

claim_recovery_table.claim: IoU threshold affects all methods similarly, with optimal around 0.3
claim_recovery_table.evidence: PARTIALLY SUPPORTED - SORT peaks at IoU=0.3, ByteTrack at IoU=0.4, SparseTrack at IoU=0.3
